passage:
Monday. Simran leaned over the partition. "We're going to the dosa place at one. Come?" Maria's cheeks warmed. She had a half-finished deck and a heavy head from a poor night. "Maybe next time," she said, and ate a sandwich at her desk.

Thursday. Simran asked again, lighter this time. Maria felt the same pull to say no and said it, then heard the group laughing by the lift and felt the office go quiet.

The following Tuesday. Simran did not ask; she just picked up her bag. "Coming?" Maria's tiredness had not gone anywhere, but she closed her laptop. Over dosas she learned Simran had also moved to the city alone, two years ago. She laughed at a story about the boss's umbrella. On the way back Simran said, "Same time Thursday?"

qa.q: Where did the group go for lunch?
qa.a: The group went to the dosa place.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling when she said "Maybe next time"?
qa.a: She felt shy and tired, with a half-finished deck and a heavy head from a poor night.

qa.q: What small step helped Maria on Tuesday?
qa.a: She said yes even though her tiredness had not gone anywhere, and she closed her laptop and went along.

qa.q: How might Simran have seen Maria's earlier refusals?
qa.a: Simran kept asking lightly and had moved to the city alone too, so Simran may have understood the hesitation rather than taking it as rejection.

grounding: A colleague invites Maria to lunch; after declining twice from shyness and tiredness she says yes and a friendship starts.

passage: Neelam, you said no to the canteen group again today; I saw. Let Trisha-aunty tell you a small thing. My first job was at a bank branch in Pune, forty years ago. A colleague named Rosy asked me to lunch on my second day. I said I'd brought tiffin. She asked the next week; I said I was tired. She asked a third time; I said maybe tomorrow, and hid in the record room. After a month she stopped asking. I ate alone for most of that year. Then one Friday I was so tired I nearly said no again, but I said yes just to stop myself. We ate vada pav on the steps. Rosy became the friend who carried my wedding sari and held my first baby. All from one tired yes. So tomorrow, when they ask, say yes, Neelam.

qa.q: What did Trisha and Rosy eat on the steps?
qa.a: They ate vada pav on the steps.

qa.q: How might young Trisha have felt hiding in the record room?
qa.a: Trisha was likely shy and anxious, avoiding the lunch even though it left her eating alone.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed Trisha's first year?
qa.a: Saying yes to Rosy on a tired Friday, which began a lifelong friendship.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Rosy when Trisha kept saying no?
qa.a: Rosy may have felt turned away and unsure whether Trisha wanted company, which is why she stopped asking after a month.

grounding: An aunt recalls declining a colleague's lunch invitations out of shyness, and how one tired yes began a lifelong friendship.

passage: It was pouring over Whitefield, Vishal had just finished a ten-hour shift fixing a server crash, and all he wanted was his bed. Then Sahil from the next desk leaned over. 'A few of us are getting biryani near the metro. Come?' Vishal had said no twice already that month: once for laundry, once because he didn't know anyone and the thought of small talk made his stomach tight. He opened his mouth to say 'next time'. Instead he heard himself say, 'Okay, give me five minutes.' The biryani place was loud and the auto ride was wet. He barely spoke for the first half hour. Then someone asked about his hometown, Jalandhar, and Sahil turned out to have cousins there. They shared an auto back. On Monday, Sahil saved him a chair at lunch.

qa.q: How long had Vishal's shift been?
qa.a: Vishal's shift had been ten hours.

qa.q: What was Vishal feeling when Sahil invited him?
qa.a: Vishal felt exhausted and anxious about small talk, tempted to say 'next time' again.

qa.q: Why was saying yes a good choice even though Vishal was tired?
qa.a: It led to a shared auto and a saved chair on Monday, the start of a friendship that more refusals would have blocked.

qa.q: How might Sahil have taken a third no from Vishal?
qa.a: Sahil might have assumed Vishal didn't want company and stopped inviting him.

grounding: Shows a tired, shy newcomer accepting a colleague's invitation in bad weather, and a friendship beginning from that yes.
